title: Naturalization - standard 5-year rule
facts: The standard naturalization path for a lawful permanent resident generally requires 5 years of permanent residence.
The applicant generally must be at least 18 and satisfy continuous residence, physical presence, local residence, and other statutory requirements.
The standard 5-year path generally requires at least 30 months of physical presence in the United States during the 5 years before filing.
Eligible applicants may file Form N-400 up to 90 calendar days before completing the continuous-residence period.
